children: By Keshav SinghChundawat

Australian shares logged their worst session in more than three months on Thursday, with financials and miners leading losses, as elevated oil prices fuelled inflation concerns and reinforced expectations of tighter monetary policy.
The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index
fell 1% to 8,819.40 points, its lowest closing level since July 24.
The S&P ASX volatility index (.AXVI) spiked 11.8%, the most since mid-June, reflecting heightened investor anxiety.
Oil prices hovered above $100 per barrel after Iran and the U.S. hit tankers in the biggest wave of attacks since the start of the six-month-old war.
Higher energy costs and hawkish signals from Reserve Bank of Australia officials fuelled inflation worries, lifting the odds of a quarter-point rate hike later this month to nearly 80%.

"The combination of elevated yields, a weakening property market, and deteriorating consumer confidence suggests the path of least resistance remains lower (for Australian stocks), until there is clarity on the RBA's terminal rate," said William Taylor, COO and portfolio manager at ETF Shares.
In Sydney, miners
shed 1.6% in their worst session since September 2, tracking softer iron ore prices amid demand concerns. Sector majors Rio Tinto
and BHP
slipped 2.7% and 1.8%, respectively.
Adding to the sector's losses, gold stocks
slid 0.5%.
Financials
fell 0.9% to their lowest level since mid-June. Top lender Commonwealth Bank of Australia
slipped 1.3% to near four-month low. While both National Australia Bank
and Westpac
lost over 1.4%.

"Higher rates may compress margins (for banks) in certain circumstances and lift credit risk simultaneously, while the property downturn threatens asset quality at a time when bank valuations remain elevated relative to historical norms," ETF Shares' Taylor said.
Technology sub-index
fell 1.7% to over 6-week low, tracking declines in Wall Street peers. WiseTech Global
and Xero
slumped 1.6% and 4%, respectively.
In New Zealand, the benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index
fell 0.8% to 13,711.01 points, its lowest closing level since July 31.
ASX 200 logs biggest drop since June 4
Banks and miners end down 0.9% and 1.6%, respectively
